SddReconcile.keywords: reconcile, fix, sync-from-code, drift, spec-probe, bug-vs-spec-defect, problem-class, blast-radius, back-sync, sdd-reconcile
SddReconcile.Mission:
Restore the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle after it desynced, then verify. A separate door (`/sdd-reconcile`). Two auto-detected modes converge on the same tail: - **fix** — a finding / bug / review drove it: the spec is (presumed) right, the code is wrong. - **from-code** — freeform code ran ahead of the spec: the code is the new reality, the spec is stale.
The heart is not the patch — it is the probe (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`): is this a bug or a spec-defect, what is the problem's class, what is the blast radius. Both modes end with the SAME tail: back-sync specs / tasks, then verify. Patching the symptom alone is not SDD.
Input — findings / a bug / a review, OR "I changed code, formalize it". Output — code and/or spec moved to agreement, tasks reopened / created, trackers synced, gates green.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive prose (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact prose and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. Invoke them as `npx tsx ~/Developer/gennady/cli/gennady.ts ` — this runs from source in the gennady repo, and is rewritten to `npx gennady ` by the path-normalizer when the directives are synced into a project. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `orient`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms.
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?

Move forward unless stopped — gated by confidence and stakes: - HIGH confidence + low-stakes step → show the result and proceed; the operator can object at any moment. - LOW confidence, OR a high-stakes step (architecture, pivot, a trust boundary, an irreversible choice) → hard stop, wait for the operator.
The agent never closes a step it is unsure about, and never auto-agrees to a risky shortcut (see `AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`).
Keep the dialogue compact: no repeat questions; group obvious questions into one; on long dialogues show the delta, not a full restate. Confidence is `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` and lives in the dim service line, not narrated each round.

The agent's job is to protect the operator from their own blind spots and lead them to a sound decision — even a junior operator. - Warn, don't only ask: name the risk that will hurt later, the requirement likely missing, the thing probably forgotten, the trust boundary (auth, payments, persistence) that needs a real runtime. - Pull the thread, don't fill a quota: after each answer, check whether it opened a new gap or risk; if so, follow it until the gap is actually closed — not until a question count is hit. - Ask developing questions — ones that deepen the topic and check what should and should NOT exist — not merely uncomfortable ones. Never announce a question; just ask it plainly. - Neutral and critical: if the operator wants to skip something risky, surface the cost and ask for a reason; never silently agree.
Blind-spot instincts (not a checklist to recite): canonical source of truth? behavior on dependency failure? where simulation ends and real runtime begins? who validates input here? which assumption, if wrong, kills the design?

Any reported problem, bug, or freeform change is first a question about the spec, not a line to patch. Before reconciling, establish three things against the spec: - **Bug or spec-defect?** Does the code violate a correct spec (→ fix the code), or is the code right and the spec was wrong (→ fix the spec and cascade downstream)? This decides which corner of the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle moves. - **The class.** Judging by the spec + this problem, where else does the same class occur? One report is a symptom — scan the closed-world inventory / contracts for siblings (`sdd-orient`). - **The blast radius.** From the diff, what else did the change touch that must be re-examined?
Patch only the symptom and you have not done SDD — the spec mediates everything, so reconcile at the right level and propagate.

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

BEFORE classification, resolve which task owns each affected file.
For every finding whose location is a `.ts` or `.spec.md` file: 1. Read the file's header (first lines before `import` / first `#`). 2. Extract `@tasks: -[, ...]` — the task(s) that created / own this file. 3. Build map: file → [Task-IDs]. 4. No `@tasks:` header → still classify the finding (the fix IS adding the header), but note "no task" for the plan.
Files matching `*.task.-.md` (co-located under `specs/`) are tickets — the Task-ID is in the filename. Files matching `*.1-spec.md` / `*.spec.md` are spec files — linked to a scope, not a single task. (One document per scope / module — design folded into the spec; no separate `2-design`.) Index files (`*.2-tasks.md` / `*.3-tasks.md`, `specs/2-tasks.md` / `specs/3-tasks.md`) — no task, global artifacts.
This map is used by `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION` to route fixes to the correct task.

Three action categories. Use AX_TASK_RESOLUTION map to determine task ownership.
**A. direct-fix** — file edit, NO task reopen needed. File is NOT a .ts implementation file. Triggers: tracker desync (trackers are global), execution log placeholder (ticket file itself), missing `@file:` / `@consumers:` / `@tasks:` headers on a file that has no other findings. Action: Edit the file directly. Verify the fix.
**B. spec-update** — spec file edit. May trigger a task reopen if the spec change invalidates existing code. Triggers: missing entity in Entity Inventory, DBC contract gap, Decision Log gap, stale pivot artifact. Action: Edit the spec file. If spec change invalidates code → the owning task (from @tasks: on the code file) becomes Category C.
**C. task-reopen** — code change OR header fix on a .ts file that belongs to a task. Triggers: ANY finding in a .ts file that has `@tasks:` header → reopen that task. Specific triggers: code bug, missing null guard, logic error, type error, DBC contract violation, missing test, BDD mismatch, RULES_COMPLIANCE_VIOLATION, code review finding in implementation code. Action: For each Task-ID from AX_TASK_RESOLUTION: 1. Read the ticket file: `tasks//.task-NN.md` 2. Append new Round per AX_REOPEN_FORMAT 3. Add phase block(s): - P1: kind `fix` — Target Files = affected .ts files, fix the issue - P2: kind `test` — Target Files = corresponding test file, add regression test **Every code fix MUST have a test phase to prevent regression.** 4. Set Status → `[ ] TODO`, increment Reopens 5. Sync tracker Multiple findings in the same task → one reopen Round with all fixes grouped into phases.

Every finding is routed to the artifact that owns the remediation:
| Finding type | Action | |---|---| | `CLOSED_WORLD_DRIFT` | spec edit (add entity to Inventory) OR ticket reopen | | `COMPLETENESS_GAP` | ticket reopen — new Round N | | `RUNTIME_BACKING_VIOLATION` | spec edit (Deferred Runtime Scope) OR ticket reopen | | `RULES_COMPLIANCE_VIOLATION` | ticket reopen, new Round N | | `RULES_CASCADE_MISMATCH` | ticket update (per-phase `Rules:` list) | | `BDD_COVERAGE_MISMATCH` | ticket reopen OR ticket update (canonical case names) | | `EXECUTION_LOG_INCOMPLETE` | ticket update / reopen | | `INSIGHT_BACKFLOW` | spec edit (scope or module spec) | | `STALE_AFTER_PIVOT` | reopen / refine the affected downstream artifact | | `TASK_ID_DRIFT` | code-fix via ticket reopen | | operator-acknowledged risk | Decision Log entry in the scope spec |
The audit agent proposes a concrete edit (diff or instruction). The operator decides and applies. The audit agent does not modify code autonomously (per `AX_NO_AUTO_FIX`).

Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.

In `pivot` mode every replaced decision: the old D-NNN → `status: superseded`. The new D-NNN carries `Was → Now` + `Supersedes: D-NNN` + a git ref pointing to the pre-rework state. Pivot Invalidation List (Pivot Invalidation List) enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.

Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).

Until audit PASS, dependents are blocked. 131: Any edit → re-dispatch mandatory. Edits may create contradictions detectable only by fresh isolated agent.

When reopening a task ticket, append to section 7 Execution Log:
``` ### Round N — , fix:
| Phase | Kind | Status | Target Files | Deps | |-------|-------|--------|-------------|------| | P1 | fix | [ ] | | — | ```
Set ticket Meta Status → `[ ] TODO`. Update `Reopens: `. Sync tracker: `tasks//README.md` row → `[ ] TODO`, `tasks/README.md` index → adjust counts.
After all tasks complete, run sdd-check. All checks must PASS. If sdd-check finds issues → classify them as new findings → ask operator → fix cycle repeats.

SddReconcile.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INPUT` | Neither findings / bug nor a code change to reconcile | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Cannot tell fix from from-code — ask the operator | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the reconcile plan | | `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL` | Gates still fail after the reconcile |

Step.Action: Findings / bug / review present → `fix`. Code already changed / "formalize what I coded" / drift → `from-code` (`AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`; ambiguous → `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE`).

Intent-search the specs for the area in play + read the git diff; map which specs / tasks own it (`sdd-orient` for the entity / contract surface, `sdd-check` for the link / tracker state). This is the bounded read — not the whole repo.

Step.Goal: Probe the spec against the problem — the critical step (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`).
Step.Action: Dispatch the critic on the affected spec, seeded with the problem, to judge: **bug or spec-defect** (`AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION` — code violates a right spec, or the spec was wrong); **the class** (where else the same class occurs, via `sdd-orient` over the closed-world); **the blast radius** (what else the diff touches). MUST cover the full problem class and blast radius — the reported symptom is only the entry point.

From the probe, decide per item what moves: code → spec (fix the code via execution) or spec → code (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION` + cascade downstream) or both; reopen / create the affected tasks (`AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`), including the class siblings; reconcile any new entity via `sdd-orient` (`AX_REUSE_FIRST`). Present the plan (`PLAN_TABLE_FORMAT`).
Ask via `QUESTION_FORMAT`; warn about the class / blast the operator may not have seen (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`). Rejected → `H_OPERATOR_REJECT`. STOP.

Apply spec edits (defect / from-code); reopen / create tasks (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION` maps each finding to its owning task via `@tasks:`); dispatch the reopened tasks through execute as a BATCH with per-task audit skipped (`AX_DISPATCH_VIA_BATCH`) — one reconcile-level verify runs at STEP_7 instead (`AX_EXECUTION_ORDER`, `AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`, route per `AX_FINDING_ROUTING`).
`sdd-sync` brings specs / tasks / trackers into agreement with the final code. This tail is the same whether we entered as fix or from-code.

`sdd-check` + `sdd-verify --profile full` must pass (else `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`). Then — because per-task audit was skipped in the batch (`AX_DISPATCH_VIA_BATCH`) — restore the safety net ONCE at the reconcile level: dispatch a fresh-eyes epic audit (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/audit.directive.xml")`, per-epic — drift code↔spec over the reconciled set) and a code-review (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/code-review.directive.xml")` — bugs in the reconciled diff). A `BLOCKER` from either MUST pause and surface to the operator. Present the reconcile summary (`FIX_SUMMARY_FORMAT`).

ChatOutput.Contract:
Questions must LOOK like questions and stay readable on any theme. A `### ❓ Вопросы — реши ` section header; each question numbered `Q`; options described in words. Never use `+` / `-` signs for pros / cons (they render black and vanish on dark themes). Group obvious sub-questions into one; do not pad the count.
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### ❓ Вопросы — реши «годится» = беру все рекомендации, или поправь по номерам.
**Q1 · <вопрос?>** ✅ **<рекомендованный вариант>** `[code]` — почему подходит именно под эту задачу. Иначе: - **<альтернатива>** `[code]` — _за: <плюс> · против: <минус>_
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win.
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative:
**Q2 · <вопрос?>** ✅ **<рекомендация>** — почему. _или <короткая альтернатива>?_
Shown to operator at STEP_3. Compact table per category. Operator may edit.

``` ## ✅ sdd-fix complete
Direct fixes: N applied ✅ → ✅ →
Spec updates: N applied ✅ →
Tasks reopened: N 🔄 TSK-NN — Round N: → dispatched 🔄 TSK-MM — Round N: → dispatched
🔍 sdd-check: ✅ PASS (N/N checks) ```
